attribution.note: Marcus states this in his own voice; it is separate from the quoted Kurzweil clarification.

semantics.note: The proposition faithfully captures the asserted insufficiency of scaling alone, understood in context as scaling LLMs to reach AGI.

contract.note: The contract reasonably interprets AGI as broad human-level cognitive competence and distinguishes scaling from substantive methodological changes. Its criteria match the categorical causal claim.

evidence.note: Dated primary scaling research measures prediction loss. Those improvements establish neither AGI nor a ceiling below human-level competence.
The cited version predates the cutoff. Its theoretical limitations do not establish a ceiling below human-level competence; unavoidable errors also constrain humans.
This timely company disclosure reports strong capabilities and multiple research ingredients. It neither independently establishes AGI nor isolates scaling as their cause.

reviews.rationale: The packet establishes neither that scaling LLMs alone cannot reach AGI nor that it has done so. Loss improvements, theoretical limitations without a human-level boundary, and company-reported capabilities from multiple methods leave the causal claim unsettled.
